section.title: Future Developments
section.p: The pmMDA has an incomplete implementation of some functions.

ul.li: The mechanism of protected area in the generated source code.
The load and save mechanisms for models works only for ArgoUML - using NSUML - and XML representation - using XStream from Codehause-. The MDR functionality is on hold until ArgoUML supports it.

section.title: Future Developments
section.p: Some pmMDA future directions are identified. Volonteers are welcome to realize these developments or define new extensions.

dl.dd: The generators templates can be extented to support C++ as a target platform. Some of the used components such as logging are available in C++. The major effort would be to port the BOG framework to C++.
Interested developers are welcome. The core team of pmMDA do not have .NET expertise.
dl.dt: Integration with open source MDA Tools
dl.dd: The open source UML tool ArgoUML is supported. The next step would be to support the product Poseidon also available as a free community edition.

section.title: Technical University Projects
section.p: pmMDA initiative was used to develop an Eclipse plugin prototype. The prototype is the result of a semester work of two students of the technical university of Raperswil, Switzerland. All feedbacks concerning the MDA model, the configuration properties and the code generator were integrated in the current release series. The pmMDA is still distributed as a standalone application to simplify its use for users not working with the Eclipse environment.

The next step is to convince technical university to use the releases published on sourceforge as a basis for bachelor and master works or as a teaching instrument when discussing UML and MDA approaches.

section.title: Industrial Projects
section.p: pmMDA was started as a pragmatic solution to solve problems of industrial and commercial projects in which the pmMDA group members were working. One major goal of the initiative is and will always be to provide pragmatic ways to use MDA paradigms on mission critical projects.

A collaboration with a major player in the reinsurance business demonstrates the adequacy of pmMDA to develop deal and contract management applications for insurance business. The application is a mission critical suite deployed worldwide and has more than seven hundred users.

A collaboraiton with a major software contracting company in Switzerland showed the efficiency of the pmMDA approach to develop and maintain complex device management applications. The mission critical application remotely manages industrial plants and devices in Europe.
